summary: Intermittent 5xx pulses correlated with accept-queue surge and ephemeral worker exhaustion
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed short (~30–90s) pulses of elevated 5xx across streaming and short-request endpoints in us-east-1. The pulses coincide with an accept-queue growth on the api-gateway and a cascade of ephemeral-worker restarts in the serving runtime.

Impact:
- Multiple requests returned 502/503/504 during the pulses across a handful of dedicated tenants (not universal).
- Increased latency for streaming sessions (stalls, reconnects).
- One customer (LumenScribe Inc.) reported bulk-embedding jobs failing mid-upload.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east-1, Dedicated pool for LumenScribe (reserved GPUs).
- Gateway version: apigw v2.18.1.
- Ephemeral proxy: proxy-v1.6.3.
- Serving runtime: runtime-3.4.7 (nvml driver 535.86).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Large customer performed a multipart embedding upload (thousands of small files uploading in parallel) while also maintaining many long-lived streaming sessions.
2) Ingress saw a sharp rise in concurrent TCP accepts and many half-open/long-lived connections.
3) api-gateway accept-queue length increased beyond configured threshold, triggering temporary prioritization/shed logic.
4) Ephemeral proxy layer experienced thread saturation; some proxies reaped connections causing upstream hedged retries to fan out to serving runtimes.
5) Serving runtime reported worker exhaustion and watchdog restarts, leading to transient 5xx waves.

Observed behavior:
- apigw logs show repeated "accept queue full" warnings and 502 for upstream reset.
- Ephemeral proxy logs show "worker-thread-starved" and "conn-hold-timeout" messages.
- Runtime logs show repeated "watchdog: worker OOM?" and subsequent clean restarts.

Expected behavior:
- Backpressure at the gateway should be signaled gracefully to the client without amplifying retries, and ephemeral proxies should avoid triggering widespread runtime fanout.

Recent changes before incident:
- Autoscaler tuning rolled out last week (staggered hotplug) to reduce GPU cold-starts (PR 4281).
- Increased default connection keepalive for streaming in apigw config (v2.18.1).

Mitigation performed so far:
- Rate limited the offending customer's multipart upload at the edge for 45 minutes (temporary hard cap).
- Manually increased accept-queue depth and temporarily disabled aggressive hedged-retry on the gateway for the tenant route.
- Restarted a subset of ephemeral proxies with threadpool=larger to reduce thread starvation.

Logs / snippets (redacted):
- apigw: [2026-03-12T22:11:08Z] WARN accept_queue length=124 (threshold=100) route=LumenScribe-embed
- apigw: [2026-03-12T22:11:09Z] ERROR proxy_upstream_reset upstream=10.0.11.23:8080 status=502
- ephemeral-proxy: [2026-03-12T22:11:10Z] ERROR worker-thread-starved tid=0x7f4c conn-count=260
- runtime: [2026-03-12T22:11:12Z] WARN watchdog: worker 23 heartbeat-miss=3 -> restarting
- runtime: [2026-03-12T22:11:12Z] ERROR runtime-exit code=137 reason="killed-by-watchdog"

Monitoring links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/ingress/accept-queue-us-east?orgId=1
- SLO/Incidents: https://status.redwood.dev/incidents/INC-20260312-27
investigation: Initial hypothesis: combination of upload fan-in + long-lived streams causing accept-queue exhaustion and amplified hedged retries into upstream runtime leading to worker exhaustion.
Correlated timestamps across apigw, proxy, and runtime logs show accept-queue growth preceding runtime watchdog restarts by ~2–6s consistently.

Heap/profile of a restarted runtime instance shows elevated file-descriptor usage and large number of inflight multiplexed streams; runtime did not OOM in memory but reported abrupt kills by watchdog (suggesting CPU/thread starvation/polling issues).
Checked autoscaler logs — no large-scale GPU preemption observed. Autoscaler activity (hotplug) occurred ~10m prior but did not correlate directly to the spike timestamp.
Telemetry: increased hedged-retry amplification factor observed for streaming routes due to default retry window increase in apigw config.
comments: Aisha Khan (support): Received customer report at 22:20 UTC — they saw ~3 short waves of 502/503; provided initial logs and request IDs.

Evan Cho (SRE): Investigating. Initial glance shows accept-queue growth on apigw and a pattern of ephemeral proxy thread saturation. Repro attempt with synthetic load shows similar accept-queue pulses when combining 1000 parallel small uploads + 200 streaming sessions.

Marco Silva (runtime): Looked at runtime core dumps — no memory OOM. Watchdog triggered because a large number of workers missed heartbeat; likely CPU starvation from syscall/poll storms. Adding to theory: many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT and long poll loops.
Priya Raman (CS): Applied a temporary soft-rate-limit on LumenScribe's tenant route to reduce upload fan-in. Customer confirmed a drop in incidents after limit applied.
Evan Cho (SRE): Pushing temporary config: reduce hedged-retry window and backoff multiplier for streaming routes in us-east. Monitoring for recurrence.
Aisha Khan (support): Customer accepted the temporary cap and asked for ETA on permanent fix. Escalated to Engineering for root-cause and regression plan.
Evan Cho (SRE): Created follow-up task to add accept-queue autoshed metrics and to harden proxy threadpool defaults. Linking RFCs.
resolution: Short-term: Applied tenant-side hard caps on parallel multipart uploads for LumenScribe and lowered hedged-retry aggressiveness for streaming routes in prod us-east-1.

Medium-term: Engineering to roll a patch that 1) adds explicit backpressure header signaling from api-gateway when accept-queue grows, 2) rate limits hedged-retries when upstreams signal high queue lengths, and 3) increases ephemeral-proxy default threadpool and adds a watchdog that drains long-held connections more gracefully.

Long-term: Autoscaler and runtime teams to run a chaos experiment and add telemetry for accept-queue backpressure propagation to prevent amplification loops. Plan an SLO change to include accept-queue thresholds in incident detection rules.
Follow-ups assigned to ENG-OPS: create PR for gateway backpressure header (PR 4387), runtime change to improve worker liveness checks (PR 4392), and a runbook update for accept-queue pulses.
workaround: Applied rate-limiting at the edge for the offending tenant and reduced hedged-retry aggressiveness. Customer resumes uploads at reduced parallelism as advised.
next_steps: ENG: Implement gateway backpressure header + hedged-retry guard (owner: Marco Silva, target: 2026-03-25).
SRE: Add accept-queue based alert to runbook and tune ephemeral-proxy threadpool defaults (owner: Evan Cho, target: 2026-03-18).
CS: Confirm customer rollback plan for resumed uploads and inform them of ETA for permanent fix (owner: Priya Raman, target: 2026-03-15).
